rv.q: This Beautiful Future defies cogent description, and it needs to be experienced to understand how the strange, disturbing, and life-affirming elements all fit perfectly together under Jack Serio's stunning direction.
This Beautiful Future is a peculiar yet quietly compelling portrait of two teenagers, a French girl and a German soldier, chasing a connection — and a roll in the hay — amid wartime.
As a workout for two fine young acting talents, This Beautiful Future has its moments.
While This Beautiful Future is tastefully presented, it does not deal with the moral issues that the play hints at but refuses to recognize.
To call it the proverbial oil-and-water mix doesn’t begin to describe this onstage mismatch.
Kalnejais may have been going for genre-defying—period drama with a contemporary Greek chorus—but the two parts don’t mesh.
I really wanted to love this play, but I found myself more impatient with it than anything else.
It is a tale overwritten, overwrought, and pretentious.

cn.t: Critics split on this WWII romance between a French girl and German soldier, with some finding it quietly compelling and shimmering, while others are left flat by its peculiar mix of wartime drama and modern elements like karaoke.
